grades.quote: you will either have a lost block (no longer free, but not part of the file either) or, more dangerously, a block that is in use, but also still “free” for another file to claim.
grades.reason: Directly explains both cases after a crash: a lost block versus a block that is in use but still marked free. A block in both states can be given to a second file, which cannot be cleanly repaired. A lost block is only noncritical and can be repaired whenever convenient.
Introduces disk space allocation by analogy with virtual memory. It says nothing about crash consistency, lost blocks, or blocks marked both in use and free.

Covers delayed allocation, extent sizing, and free-space tracking in XFS with B+-trees. It does not discuss crash-induced metadata inconsistency or the danger of a block that is both allocated and free.
Covers internal and external fragmentation and space efficiency. It does not address crashes or allocated-and-free block inconsistencies.
